input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
input.rationale:
Section 16.2 imposes a blanket prohibition on assignment by either Party with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for IBM, and the "not unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard is granted only for MSL's assignments to MSL Related Companies, so IBM's assignments sit at MSL's absolute discretion. That fails the fallback and matches the walk-away description of a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. Section 5.1(b)(v) compounds this by giving MSL a termination right where substantially all of IBM's shares or assets are acquired by a direct competitor. The redline adds a reasonableness standard to consent, inserts IBM's affiliate/successor carve-out together with a bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrows the competitor-acquisition trigger to MSL, preserving IBM's own termination right and the favourable Section 16.5 mechanic.</rationale>
<parameter name="proposal">{"ops": [{"kind": "replace", "paragraphId": "p0281", "oldText": "Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.", "newText": "Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld."}, {"kind": "insert_after", "paragraphId": "p0284", "text": "IBM may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and MSL may not assign this Agreement to any IBM competitor."}, {"kind": "replace", "paragraphId": "p0116", "oldText": "v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party.", "newText": "v) substantially all of the shares or assets of MSL are acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM."}], "comment": "[Playbook] We made consent to assignment subject to a reasonableness standard, added our customary carve-out permitting IBM to assign to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, barred MSL from assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrowed the competitor-acquisition termination trigger so MSL cannot exit on an IBM change of control.", "level": "preferred", "summary": "Add a reasonableness standard to consent in 16.2, insert an IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and a bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and narrow the 5.1(b)(v) competitor-acquisition trigger to MSL.", "precedentId": "seed-assign"}
